name: t5probe_c
description: Phase 3 T5 PROBE -- CANDIDATE C. Throwaway 1 km probe run, not a shippable scenario: it exists to answer the multicell initiation question against the classifier pre-registered in docs/phase3-t5-multicell.md §3, which was committed before this config was written. Expected: squall-line / MCS organisation. Same RKW88 profile as B but initiated with iinit=8, the line thermal with random perturbations -- x-centred with no y term in its beta, so it spans the full y extent at any domain size (unlike iinit=3, whose bubble positions are hardcoded). irandp=0, CORRECTED before this probe ran (docs §6.2): the first draft set irandp=1 on the reasoning that random_seed(put=) sits inside IF(irandp.eq.1) and so is what seeds the generator iinit=8 draws from. True, but irrelevant -- gfortran's random_number is deterministically seeded without that call, so iinit=8 gets its noise either way -- and irandp=1 would ALSO sprinkle +-0.25 K over the ENTIRE domain at t=0, which in the low-CIN WK sounding grows spurious secondary cells near the boundaries (measured in T4's t4gate_sc run: 4 of 6 cells at t=120 sat 4-14 km from the east wall, 76-86 km from the storm). Those would inflate M2/M3 and could return a FALSE MULTICELL -- the classifier would be right about the count and wrong about the storm. Any multicellularity here must come from the line thermal and the cold pool (charter principle 1), never from domain-wide noise. Probe geometry is T4 §5.2's: 180x180 @ 999 m = 179.82 km, 2 h, dtl=6, ~13 min per run instead of ~4.5 h at 333 m. The 1 km caveat is stated in docs §6.1 -- component counts may bias low; the REGIME call is what survives at this resolution.
